**Answer: r = 1037**

Let p = 2027. Since the coefficients of f have denominators that are products of differences of the points 1, …, p, none of which is divisible by p, f has p-integral coefficients. So the requested r is the coefficient of x^{2025} reduced mod p, and we can compute the interpolant over F_p.

**Step 1: Write f over F_p.** For x in F_p, (x − n)^{p−1} equals 1 when x ≠ n and 0 when x = n. So 1 − (x − n)^{p−1} is the indicator of x = n. Summing over the set S of perfect squares in {1, …, p}:

$$f(x) \equiv \sum_{n\in S}\bigl(1-(x-n)^{p-1}\bigr) \pmod p.$$

This has degree p − 1 = 2026, so it is the required interpolant.

**Step 2: Extract the coefficient of x^{p−2}.** The constant terms contribute nothing to x^{p−2}. From −(x − n)^{p−1}, the x^{p−2} term is

$$-\binom{p-1}{p-2}(-n) = -(p-1)(-n) \equiv -(-1)(-n) = -n.$$

So the coefficient of x^{2025} is −Σ_{n∈S} n (mod p).

**Step 3: Sum the squares.** The squares in {1, …, 2027} are k² for k = 1, …, 45, since 45² = 2025 and 46² = 2116 > 2027. Their sum is

$$\sum_{k=1}^{45} k^2 = \frac{45\cdot 46\cdot 91}{6} = 31395.$$

Reducing mod 2027: 31395 − 15·2027 = 31395 − 30405 = 990.

**Step 4: Combine.** The coefficient is ≡ −990 ≡ 1037 (mod 2027). Since a/b ≡ 1037 (mod 2027), we have a ≡ 1037·b, so r = 1037.

ANSWER: 1037
